$schema.description: The schema to validate this document against.

endian.description: Which byte order to use when parsing/generating machine code and binary data.

byte_order.description: Which byte order to use when parsing/generating machine code and binary data.

project_directory_is_cwd.description: When enabled, changes the current working directory at runtime to the project directory. Otherwise, the current working directory will simply be the directory in which seaside was invoked.

features.description: Customizes the features available to the seaside engine.

kernel_space_accessible.description: Allow users to provide code and/or data relating to kernel space.

self_modifying_code.description: Enable run-time modification of text segments (.text and .ktext).

delay_slot.description:
Simulate the delay slot.

As of seaside v1.2.0, this setting does nothing, but support for this feature will eventually be introduced.

freeable_heap_allocations.description: Allow sbrk to free memory when given a negative argument.

show_crash_handler.description:
Enable the displaying of a crash handler when an unhandled exception is thrown.

The crash handler is inspired by the N64's crash handler, in case you were wondering.

assembler.description: Set features available to the assembler.

pseudo_instructions.description:
Allow use of pseudo-instructions and formats.

As of seaside v1.2.0, this setting does nothing, but support for this feature will eventually be introduced.

system_services.description:
Set system services available to the interpreter.

Attempting to call an unmapped service will result in a SyscallFailure exception. The same goes for services that haven't been implemented, even if they are mapped.

syscalls.description:
Set system services available to the interpreter.

Attempting to call an unmapped service will result in a SyscallFailure exception. The same goes for services that haven't been implemented, even if they are mapped.

memory_map.description: Maps various memory regions to address ranges. This information is crucial for initializing the interpreter.

exception_handler.description: The address of the exception handler, which must reside in the .ktext segment.

user_space.description:
The memory addresses available to an ordinary user.

This range must not overlap with kernel_space. If it does, seaside will throw a fatal error on startup.

kernel_space.description:
The memory addresses available exclusively to the kernel.

This range must not overlap with user_space. If it does, seaside will throw a fatal error on startup.

segments.description: Specifies the address ranges and allocated sizes of various segments.

stack_and_heap.description: The portion of memory in which the stack and heap live.

range.description: The range of addresses this segment contains.

allocate_stack.description: The maximum number of bytes to allocate for the stack at runtime.

allocate_heap.description: The maximum number of bytes to allocate for the heap at runtime.

items.description: The inclusive minimum of the range.
The inclusive maximum of the range.
